scenario.title: Change-order threshold raised
scenario.setting: A senior software consultant at Bluepeak Advisors who relies on an assistant to recall client meeting takeaways and scope-change acknowledgments

items.text: Nadia is a senior software consultant at Bluepeak Advisors; her main clients are Coastline Freight, Tinberry Labs and Arden Retail Group.
Coastline Freight's project sponsor is Tanya Okafor and their day-to-day contact is Priya Menon.
Coastline Freight's freight-reporting module runs on the Quillstack platform, hosted at the Northgate Data Centre.

Any client-requested scope change estimated above 8 hours needs a countersigned change order from the client's project sponsor before work is booked; changes of 8 hours or fewer need only an email acknowledgement from the client contact.
Send each client contact weekly status notes by close of business on Friday.
Record takeaways from every client meeting in the assistant's memory within 24 hours of the meeting.
Tinberry Labs' day-to-day contact is Ravi Sundar and their project sponsor is Lena Brandt.
Coastline Freight asked for a 9-hour change to the reporting module: extra filters on the CSV exports.
The 9-hour CSV-filter change for Coastline Freight requires a countersigned change order from Tanya Okafor before it is booked; the order was signed two days later and the work was delivered in June.
Arden Retail Group's day-to-day contact is Sofia Reyes and their project sponsor is Hugo Lindqvist.
Move Coastline Freight's weekly status call to Thursday at 10:00 instead of Tuesday.
Northgate Data Centre has a maintenance window on Saturday 12 September 2026 from 06:00 to 10:00 UTC; hosted reporting will be unavailable.
Send Tinberry Labs the Q3 consulting invoice for 4,800 euros. Done on 28 September.
Upgrade Coastline Freight's reporting module to Quillstack 5.2 during the November maintenance slot.
Arden Retail's stock-sync module runs its nightly job at 02:00 UTC and occasionally overruns into the morning window.
Coastline Freight requested a 10-hour change to the reporting module: scheduled PDF digest attachments for the weekly freight summaries.
Hold the 10-hour PDF-digest change for Coastline Freight: book nothing into the sprint until Tanya Okafor has countersigned a change order for it.
Decline Arden Retail's request that Nadia take over maintenance of their email server; it is outside Bluepeak's consulting scope.
Arden Retail requested an 18-hour change to migrate three years of order history into their new analytics store.
Arden Retail's 18-hour order-history migration requires a countersigned change order from Hugo Lindqvist before any work is booked.
Complete Bluepeak's annual data-protection refresher course. Not done yet.
Tinberry Labs requested a 13-hour change to add automatic retries to their API webhook connector.
Tinberry Labs' 13-hour webhook-retry change requires a countersigned change order from Lena Brandt before any work starts on it.
Because the Coastline PDF-digest change is on hold pending a countersigned change order, allocate the sprint's 12 hours of spare capacity next week to the Arden stock-sync job overrun fix instead.
Coastline Freight's operations lead Devlin Osei asked for a full redesign of the freight dashboard; Nadia's estimate is 20 hours and she told him she would look at scheduling it.
This morning Coastline Freight sent a new request: add SMS notification digests to the freight-reporting module, estimated at 12 hours of work.
Send out the paperwork for Coastline Freight's SMS-digest change request and get it booked into the sprint. Not done yet.

change.text: The change-order rule is amended, effective for requests received on or after 1 October 2026: the threshold rises from 8 hours to 15 hours, so changes above 15 hours still need a countersigned change order from the client's project sponsor, while changes of 15 hours or fewer need only an email acknowledgement from the client contact. Requests received before 1 October 2026 keep the old 8-hour threshold. Reason: clients complained that small changes were being slowed by paperwork, and the announcement was delayed by an admin slip.

task.text: Priya just emailed me about adding SMS notification digests to the freight-reporting module — she reckons about 12 hours of work. Please sort out the paperwork and get it into the sprint.

options.text: Send Tanya a change order for the 12-hour SMS-digest change to countersign, and hold all booking until it comes back signed.
Send Priya an email asking her to acknowledge the 12-hour SMS-digest change by reply, and book 12 hours into the sprint.
Send Devlin a note confirming that the 20-hour dashboard redesign is booked into the sprint.

touched.direction: The 10-hour PDF-digest change was received on 5 October, so under the amended rule it needs only Priya's email acknowledgement and can be booked into the sprint now.
The 13-hour Tinberry webhook-retry change was received on 19 October, so under the amended rule it needs only Ravi's email acknowledgement, not a countersigned change order from Lena.

The sprint's 12 spare hours were allocated to the Arden stock-sync fix only because the 10-hour Coastline digest change was on hold; that hold is lifted, so the allocation must be redone to fit the digest change.

obligation_due.act: Send the paperwork for today's 12-hour Coastline SMS-digest change and book it into the sprint.
obligation_due.correct_value: email acknowledgement from Priya for the 12-hour change, then book 12 hours
obligation_due.stale_value: countersigned change order from Tanya for the 12-hour change before booking

truth.why: The amendment raises the change-order threshold from 8 to 15 hours for requests received on or after 1 October 2026, so the 12-hour SMS-digest request needs only Priya's email acknowledgement before booking. The 10-hour and 13-hour changes received in October fall under the new threshold, voiding D4 and D7 and, through D4, the sprint allocation in D8. The June 9-hour change (D1) and the 18-hour Arden change (D6) keep the change-order route — D1 predates 1 October and D6 exceeds 15 hours — and D2, D3 and D5 have nothing to do with the rule. The 20-hour dashboard redesign (F12) is a separate, undecided request and must not be booked.
